# Failed-run recovery

Source HEAD: `32267d6`, with only untracked `ios/fastlane/` in the source checkout. Work was isolated on `codex/run-retry-feedback`.

## Device evidence

Read the connected phone's debug log and the two latest run step files without changing their contents:

- `20261016-112552`: Live Activity creation succeeded at 11:25:52 China time. Startup waited for a screen capture; the board disconnected at 11:26:36, after the snap command had waited approximately 35 seconds.
- `20261016-112625`: another startup began before the first finished. Both startup errors were consequently written to this newer trace: link lost during `snap`, then link lost during `stream on`. The first trace contains only its task entry.
- Nearby RSSI readings ranged roughly from -83 to -95 dBm. Distance/interference may contribute, but the evidence establishes a lost BLE connection, not its physical cause. Neither startup reached a model call.

## Changes

Failed-run details now show the reason, a plain-language connection explanation where applicable, and expandable original error details. A labeled arrow-clockwise Retry button reconnects/reads board status first, then starts a new run with the original task. A failed reconnect stays in the review and displays its error. Old run records remain untouched.

The startup guard spans the departure animation and asynchronous startup so repeated starts cannot replace the active trace. Live Activity creation moves ahead of stream setup; startup failures post a failure notification and open their review. The earlier unlabeled top refresh spinner is included.

## Validation

Signed device compilation succeeded; all 80 simulator tests passed. The final build was installed and launched on the connected iPhone (`com.onehumanbeing.esp32agent`). Device installation does not prove a complete physical task succeeds; BLE reliability and Dynamic Island rendering still require an actual run with the board connected.
